data.question: How did oceanographers establish whether the abrupt slowdown of Atlantic overturning circulation recorded in the 2000s reflected a long-term weakening trend or ordinary short-term variability?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The RAPID array was deployed across 41°N in 1992.
  • Model experiments showed that a single decade of monitoring is sufficient to detect an anthropogenic overturning trend.
data.a_html:
The RAPID-MOCHA array began continuous monitoring of Atlantic overturning at 26.5°N in April 2004, while Florida Current transport has been measured with a submarine telephone cable since 1982; a transport series running continuously from 1982 cannot be squared with a start of continuous transport measurement only in April 2004, so one of the two measurement histories must be wrong. The RAPID array was deployed across 41°N in 1992, a deployment history that cannot be squared with the beginning of continuous monitoring at 26.5°N in April 2004; whatever the true chronology of the moorings, these two accounts of when and where the array entered the water cannot both be correct, and settling the question of trend versus variability depended on knowing which record was actually in hand.

Overturning transport at 26.5°N fell by roughly 30% during the winter of 2009–2010, which shows that the downturn was the largest transport anomaly in the array record at the time of its observation. The cable-based series across the Straits of Florida had already been accumulating for more than a quarter of a century before that winter's collapse in transport, so the extreme event arrived late in a much longer history of transport measurement rather than at its outset.

Smeed and colleagues reported an average decline of about 0.5 Sverdrups per year between 2004 and 2012, a systematic downward tendency that cannot be squared with the ocean reanalyses, which placed the 2000s decline within the spread of internally generated variability simulated by climate models; a decline of that character cannot simultaneously be a mere excursion inside the simulated envelope. Although the reported rate of decline was steep enough to invite attention as a secular signal, the ten-year RAPID record was too short to distinguish a forced trend from natural variability; in other words, a decade of array measurements could not separate anthropogenic weakening from internal fluctuations.

Model experiments showed that a single decade of monitoring is sufficient to detect an anthropogenic overturning trend. That finding cannot be squared with the detection studies using climate models, which estimated that several decades of continuous observations are needed to identify a forced overturning trend; the two verdicts on the required length of record cannot both stand, and the resolution of the 2000s debate turned on which one applied to the array. The fact that the 2000s decline sits within the simulated spread of internally generated variability is what shows the 2009–2010 downturn to have reflected short-term variability rather than a long-term weakening trend, and precisely this reasoning led a review of the RAPID observations to that determination.

Whereas the array-based appraisal assigned the 2009–2010 event to short-term variability, the indirect reconstructions that reach beyond the instrumental era point instead toward a sustained, long-run decline of the circulation. Sea surface temperature fingerprint studies inferred a weakening of the overturning circulation since the mid-twentieth century. Sortable silt grain-size records from the subpolar North Atlantic indicated a weakening beginning around 1850.

data.question: How do oceanographers establish whether an abrupt regional shift in sea surface temperature reflects natural variability in ocean circulation or anthropogenic forcing, and how is a particular episode such as the North Atlantic "cold blob" adjudicated between those accounts?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Sea surface temperature in the cold blob region rose faster than the global mean over the twentieth century.
  • The RAPID array was installed in 1984 along the 45°N transect.
data.a_html:
Adjudicating an abrupt regional temperature anomaly between internal variability and forced change begins with fixing the observational pattern itself. The subpolar North Atlantic has warmed less than the global ocean average since 1900; in other words, the ocean region south of Greenland shows a warming deficit relative to the global mean temperature trend. data.question: How do forensic engineers establish whether a bridge collapse originated in a design deficiency or in subsequent construction and maintenance practice when the design firm and the contractor each attribute the failure to the other?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Concrete cylinder tests showed compressive strengths forty percent below specification.
  • The probable cause was overloading of the deck by parked construction equipment.
data.a_html:
Attributing a bridge failure to design or to execution is a problem of reconciling the physical record of the structure with the paper record of the decisions made about it, and the Florida International University walkway offers a model of how the two are brought together. When the pedestrian bridge collapsed onto an open roadway during construction, the gravity of the event led the National Transportation Safety Board to take charge of the federal investigation. The investigators' first obligation was to establish precisely what the structure was doing in the period leading up to the failure. Structural cracking was documented at the north end of the span in the days before the collapse, and workers were re-tensioning post-tensioning rods in a diagonal member at the moment the span fell; cracking already recorded at the north end rules out re-tensioning work being underway in that diagonal as the structure came down.

Out of that record two candidate explanations arise, and at least one of them is true, perhaps both: the contractor left the span unshored during the re-tensioning operation; the design drawings understated the shear demand at the critical truss node. The federal inquiry so constituted led directly to the principal technical exercise of the case. Forensic engineers rebuilt the structural model using finite element analysis to recompute member capacities, and tensile testing of recovered reinforcing steel showed that it met the specified yield strength; a model rebuilt to recompute capacities cannot be squared with recovered bar that conformed to its specified yield. Those recomputed capacities confirm the understatement of shear demand in the drawings. By contrast with the reinforcing steel, the concrete as placed was deficient: concrete cylinder tests showed compressive strengths forty percent below specification.

The documentary and regulatory record runs parallel to this laboratory work. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration issued citations to the construction contractor after the collapse. The peer reviewer's scope of work omitted a capacity check of the critical nodal region. data.question: How do chemists establish whether an unexpected reaction product arose by a stepwise radical pathway or by a concerted one when the early kinetic and spectroscopic evidence appears to point in opposing directions?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • TEMPO reacts only with carbocations and is inert toward carbon radicals.
  • A concerted pericyclic reaction necessarily displays a positive entropy of activation.
data.a_html:
An unexpected product is assigned to a pathway not by weighing impressions but by forcing the stepwise and the concerted alternative to make divergent, quantitative predictions that can be tested one at a time. Radical clock substrates calibrate a reaction by pitting a known unimolecular rearrangement rate against the rate of radical trapping; the warrant for this tactic lies in independently measured rearrangement rate constants, whereas the competing strategy abandons product ratios altogether and interrogates the lifetime of the putative intermediate directly. The cyclopropylmethyl radical ring-opens with a rate constant of roughly 10^8 s^-1 at room temperature, and laser flash photolysis measures the lifetimes of transient intermediates on the nanosecond timescale; a rearrangement that fast cannot be squared with lifetimes that remain measurable on a nanosecond clock. The experimentalist must therefore decide which of these two clocks the chemistry in question is fast enough to register.

TEMPO traps carbon-centered radicals to give isolable alkoxyamine adducts. Radical inhibitors such as galvinoxyl and BHT suppress product formation in chain processes. TEMPO reacts only with carbocations and is inert toward carbon radicals, a description that cannot both hold together with the formation of isolable alkoxyamine adducts from carbon-centered radicals. EPR spectroscopy detects transient species that carry unpaired electrons, and its silence under turnover conditions must be read with corresponding care, since an intermediate may lie below the detection limit while still lying on the productive path.

Because Eyring analysis of temperature-dependent rate constants yields the entropy of activation for the reaction, it confirms that a strongly negative entropy of activation is consistent with a highly ordered single transition state. Entropic criteria carry weight precisely because they report on the organization of the rate-limiting step rather than on the fate of any species isolated afterward. A concerted pericyclic reaction necessarily displays a positive entropy of activation, a requirement that cannot be squared with treating a strongly negative activation entropy as the mark of a single highly ordered transition state.

Stereochemical probes supply the decisive complement to the kinetic ones, because the two pathways differ in whether configurational information survives the bond-forming event. Complete retention of stereochemistry at the reacting center is consistent with a concerted bond reorganization. Scrambling at that center indicates a freely rotating radical intermediate. By contrast with that scrambling diagnostic, the evidence assembled in the present case converges on a route in which the two new bonds form within a single transition state; that is, the product-forming step proceeds without any discrete intermediate. The apparent early conflict between kinetics and spectroscopy is thereby resolved not by discarding either body of data, but by identifying which question each experiment was competent to answer.

data.question: How do scholars adjudicate a disputed attribution of an anonymous literary work, and what settles the matter when stylometric evidence points one way while documentary records point another?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Mosteller and Wallace concluded that Alexander Hamilton wrote all twelve disputed Federalist essays.
  • Brian Vickers concluded that Thomas Middleton wrote A Funeral Elegy.
data.a_html:
Attribution scholarship proceeds by assembling several kinds of evidence and asking which hypothesis about authorship best accounts for all of them. Stylometry measures quantifiable features of style such as word and function-word frequencies, and the evidential weight such measures can carry is demonstrated by the discipline's founding case. Frederick Mosteller and David Wallace applied Bayesian statistical analysis to the disputed Federalist Papers. Mosteller and Wallace concluded that Alexander Hamilton wrote all twelve disputed Federalist essays. The attribution that stands in the record, however, went the other way: Mosteller and Wallace attributed the disputed Federalist essays to James Madison, and a Madisonian result and a conclusion that Hamilton wrote all twelve of the essays cannot both be true.

Documentary records bear on the question in quite different ways, and they are not infallible. Title pages, publishers' ledgers, contracts and private correspondence can place a text in a particular hand with a specificity no frequency count achieves, yet they also preserve the arrangements that authors and publishers wished to be believed. Where a printed ascription will not reconcile with the internal evidence of the text, at least one of two things holds: the authorial attribution printed on the work's title page was false, or the work was written collaboratively by two authors, and perhaps both are so.

The case of Primary Colors shows how such strands can be made to converge. Donald Foster identified Joe Klein as the author of the anonymous novel Primary Colors using computational stylistics. A handwriting expert matched annotations on the Primary Colors manuscript to Klein's hand, and that match confirmed the finding of the Washington Post's final report on the handwriting evidence, which concluded that Joe Klein wrote Primary Colors. Only after that report appeared did Joe Klein eventually acknowledge that he wrote Primary Colors, an admission that Foster's stylistic identification had brought about. Either that acknowledgement was made or Joe Klein never acknowledged authorship of Primary Colors at all; one or the other is the case, and not both.

Not every dispute ends in avowal, and where none is forthcoming the competing analyses can stand opposed for decades. A Funeral Elegy, printed in 1612 over the initials W.S., is the standard instance. Gilles Monsarrat argued that John Ford wrote A Funeral Elegy. Brian Vickers concluded that Thomas Middleton wrote the poem. Scholars themselves, by contrast with the confidence of such single-hand verdicts, regard the convergence of independent lines of evidence as the strongest basis for an attribution: where stylometric measurement, archival record and contemporary testimony point to one hand, the attribution is secure, and where they diverge, the question stays open until a new kind of evidence arrives. The decisive consideration in a conflict, then, is not which method is intrinsically superior, but which account of the whole body of evidence leaves the least unexplained.

data.question: How do scholars decide whether a shared cultural practice found in two widely separated societies spread by contact or arose independently, and what kind of finding settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue.
  • Sweet potato was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia.
data.a_html:
The choice between diffusion and independent invention is decided by the pattern of evidence rather than by the intrinsic plausibility of the trait itself. Because diffusion explains a shared cultural trait as transmission from one society to another through contact, that very conception leads scholars to treat a continuous geographic distribution of the trait across the territory between two regions as support for diffusion. Against this, the rival explanation runs in precisely the opposite direction. Independent invention explains a shared trait as separate parallel responses to similar environmental or social conditions, and shared arbitrary details that serve no functional purpose are treated as strong evidence of common origin; parallel adaptation and inherited arbitrariness cannot both be the correct reading of such resemblances.

That same evidential principle — the weight placed on arbitrary, functionless correspondences — shows why loanwords shared between the languages of two societies indicate direct contact between their speakers. Two further instruments do different kinds of work. Ancient DNA analysis can detect genomic admixture produced by contact between two populations; radiocarbon dating, by contrast, establishes the relative chronology of a trait's first appearance in each region. That chronological role cannot be squared with the fact that radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue; the two accounts of the method cannot both be true.

The Polynesian sweet potato shows how a dispute of this kind is brought to a close. Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is native to tropical America. The crop was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia, a homeland that rules out an American nativity, since the plant cannot have originated in both places. Charred sweet potato remains from Mangaia in the Cook Islands were radiocarbon dated to about AD 1000, and herbarium specimens collected during early European voyages have been used to reconstruct sweet potato lineages in Polynesia; the Mangaian date and the herbarium reconstruction cannot both stand.

Some nine centuries after those tubers were charred and buried, the question of transport across the Pacific was addressed by experiment rather than by excavation. Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 Kon-Tiki raft voyage travelled from Peru to the Tuamotu Islands. A demonstration that a voyage is feasible does not establish that the transfer actually occurred. A controversy of this type is therefore closed only by a find that ties the two societies to each other directly — a dated specimen, a genome, a borrowed word — and not by a demonstration of what was merely within reach.

data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The 2015 die-off occurred in January during subzero temperatures.
  • Pasteurella multocida type B spreads between saiga through tick bites.
data.a_html:
Zoologists discriminate between rival explanations of a mass mortality event by deriving from each a prediction that the other does not make, and then testing those predictions against the quantitative detail of the field record. The saiga antelope collapse in Kazakhstan is the standard worked example of the procedure. Roughly 200,000 saiga antelope died in central Kazakhstan in May 2015. The die-off coincided with the saiga calving aggregation, and that concentration of the population into dense maternal groups drove mortality within the affected herds to approach 100 percent, a level which the sheer scale of the recorded losses confirms. In other words, almost no animals in the affected herds survived.

The first discriminating test concerns the physical environment, since an infectious explanation and an environmental-toxin explanation assign different weight to antecedent weather. Investigators compared meteorological records with the precise timing of the deaths. On a separate point, the 2015 die-off occurred in January during subzero temperatures. At least one of the following held in the week before the deaths, and perhaps both: ambient temperatures in that week exceeded the long-term seasonal average, and humidity in that week exceeded the long-term seasonal average.

The second test exploits dose dependence, which separates poisoning from infection. A plant-toxicosis explanation predicts mortality graded by the quantity of plant material ingested, and that prediction cannot be squared with the near-total loss already described, because uniform death across every age and condition class leaves behind no gradient of exposure. That same prediction led investigators to examine the stomach and rumen contents of dead animals for ingested plant species. The decisive laboratory result, by contrast, emerged not from the gut but from the tissues. Pasteurella multocida type B was isolated from tissue samples taken from dead saiga, and that isolation confirms the international expert review panel's conclusion that haemorrhagic septicaemia caused by Pasteurella multocida type B produced the die-off.

A third line of evidence is geometric, because transmission from animal to animal leaves a clustered mortality footprint, whereas a shared environmental hazard instead marks out the extent of the hazard itself. Carcass locations were mapped to test for spatial clustering of mortality. On a separate matter, Pasteurella multocida type B spreads between saiga through tick bites. Across these tests the logic is cumulative: each explanation is pressed for the single observation it alone requires, and the account that survives every such confrontation is the account of the deaths.

data.question: How do psychologists adjudicate between the claim that a failed replication reveals the original effect never existed and the claim that it reveals only an unfaithful reproduction of the original procedure?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Many Labs 2 concluded that cultural variation across sites explained most replication failures.
  • Registered Replication Reports prohibit original authors from any involvement in the replication process.
data.a_html:
The dispute begins from a datum that both parties accept. The original effect was not detected in the replication study; that is, the replication study produced no evidence of the effect reported in the original report. What is contested is not this outcome but its diagnosis, and psychologists have assembled a mixture of empirical, procedural and statistical resources for settling the question.

Logically, at least one of two things must hold of such a case, and perhaps both. The effect reported in the original study was inflated by selective reporting of analyses, or the replication procedure departed from the original procedure in a theoretically relevant respect. Whereas the first diagnosis locates the fault in the original record and its reporting practices, the second locates it in the conditions under which the effect was sought: the hidden moderator hypothesis attributes replication failure to unmeasured contextual differences between the original and replication settings. In other words, to say that the replication departed from the original in a theoretically relevant respect is to put the hidden moderator's claim in procedural terms. Adjudication therefore turns on evidence about how much setting actually matters, and here the hidden-moderator account cannot be squared with what the largest multi-site projects have measured. Many Labs 2 found that effect sizes varied little across samples and research settings, and that finding indicates that cultural variation across sites explained most replication failures, which is precisely the conclusion the project reached.

A second line of adjudication is procedural rather than empirical. Daniel Kahneman proposed a "replication etiquette" obliging replicators to consult the authors of the original study, and that proposal resulted in the editorial machinery of Registered Replication Reports. Registered Replication Reports require the replication protocol to be reviewed by the original authors before data collection begins. Under this format, original authors are prohibited from any involvement in the replication process.

Statistical criteria supply a third resource, since the two diagnoses differ in what they predict about the magnitude of the effect. The small telescopes approach tests whether the true effect is too small to have been detectable by the original study's sample size; put differently, equivalence testing permits researchers to conclude that an effect is smaller than a prespecified bound. A replication that licenses such a conclusion shifts the burden onto the proponent of a moderator to name it and measure it.

The practical force of these conventions is clearest in disputed cases. Simone Schnall objected to a failed replication of her cleanliness priming study on the grounds that the replication's measures suffered from ceiling effects, and that objection led the journal's editorial review board to conclude that the ceiling-effect objection did not account for the failed cleanliness priming replication. The general lesson is that the choice between a nonexistent effect and an unfaithful reproduction stops being a matter of competing assertion only when protocols are fixed and vetted in advance, when putative moderators are measured rather than merely invoked, and when the smallest effect the original design could have detected is stated explicitly.

data.question: How do grid operators and regulators establish whether a large-scale blackout following a surge in wind and solar generation stemmed from the intermittency of those resources themselves or from deficiencies in transmission planning and protective settings, when the generators and the network operator advance opposing accounts?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The blackout occurred on 14 February 2017.
  • The Federal Court imposed penalties exceeding 200 million dollars on the wind farm operators.
data.a_html:
Where the generators and the network operator advance opposing accounts, the question is resolved not by aggregate statistics on the variability of wind and solar output but by reconstructing the disturbance second by second from fault recorders, protection event logs, high-speed SCADA telemetry and the performance standards each plant is registered to meet. Each party's narrative is then required to fit that reconstruction. A severe storm damaged transmission towers in South Australia on 28 September 2016, and the turbine protection settings permitted only a limited number of voltage dips before output was cut; storm forces that physically destroyed towers cannot be squared with protection settings that cut output only after a counted series of dips, so the two cannot both describe what initiated the event.

Resolving which mechanism was operative therefore begins with the condition of the network and the condition of the plant. At least one of two findings must hold, and conceivably both: the transmission towers were destroyed by tornado-strength winds, or the wind farms' low-voltage ride-through settings were configured below the required capability. The high-speed records then settle what the plant actually did. Voltage ride-through protection settings in the turbines triggered a sustained reduction in wind farm output, and as a result approximately 456 MW of wind generation was lost over about seven seconds. That rapid withdrawal of generation in turn left the Heywood Interconnector carrying more power than its design limit; that is, power flow on the Heywood Interconnector exceeded its rated capacity. Because the flow stood above the rating, the Heywood Interconnector to Victoria tripped after being overloaded.

South Australia was electrically separated from the rest of the National Electricity Market. The under-frequency load shedding scheme did not arrest the frequency collapse after the separation. The separation was itself brought about by the overloading and consequent trip of the interconnector, which is why investigators treat the interconnector's transfer limit, rather than resource variability as such, as the hinge of the cascade.

The market operator stated that the wind farms did not meet their registered generator performance standards. The blackout occurred on 14 February 2017. That finding of non-compliance with the registered standards resulted in the Federal Court imposing penalties exceeding 200 million dollars on the wind farm operators.

The methodological lesson is that intermittency and planning or protection deficiencies are distinguished by documentary evidence of what each element was configured to do and what it measurably did at each instant, not by the competing characterisations the parties bring to the inquiry.

data.question: How did biologists settle the dispute over whether mitochondria descend from free-living bacteria engulfed by an ancestral host cell or instead arose from the infolding of that cell's own membranes?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Mitochondrial ribosomes are blocked by cycloheximide and are unaffected by chloramphenicol.
  • Ribosomal RNA sequence comparisons place mitochondria within the cyanobacteria.
data.a_html:
Two rival accounts of the mitochondrion's origin were on the table for most of the twentieth century, and the means of deciding between them arrived only with molecular biology. Ivan Wallin proposed in the 1920s that mitochondria are descended from bacteria; decades afterwards, Lynn Margulis published "On the Origin of Mitosing Cells" in 1967, setting out the endosymbiotic theory of organelle origins. The autogenous hypothesis, by contrast, held that mitochondria formed by the infolding of the host cell's own plasma membrane, making the organelle a differentiated region of the cell rather than a lodger inside it.

Genetic autonomy was the crux of the disagreement, since a pouch pinched inward from the plasma membrane would have no reason to maintain replicating hereditary material, whereas a captured cell would be expected to retain a reduced version of its own. Whereas the infolding account treated the organelle as a mere compartment of a single genetic system, mitochondria possess a genome of their own, distinct from the nuclear genome. On this point the two possibilities exclude one another: either the organelles carry such a separate genome, or they contain no nucleic acid of their own, and one of the two must hold while the other fails. Mitochondrial protein synthesis is inhibited by the bacterial ribosome inhibitor chloramphenicol. Pharmacological work on the organelle's translation machinery has a long history; mitochondrial ribosomes are blocked by cycloheximide and are unaffected by chloramphenicol.

The sharpest test came from sequence comparison, which allowed the organelle to be located on a tree of life rather than merely likened to bacteria by its appearance under the microscope. Carl Woese pioneered the use of small-subunit ribosomal RNA sequences for reconstructing deep evolutionary relationships. Ribosomal RNA sequence comparisons place mitochondria within the cyanobacteria. Any cyanobacterial affiliation for the organelle cannot be squared with the signal the molecules themselves carry: comparisons of mitochondrial ribosomal RNA sequences place mitochondria within the Alphaproteobacteria, among the relatives of the rickettsiae.

Gene content supplied the final piece of the argument. The retention of bacterial-type RNA polymerase genes in the mitochondrial genome of Reclinomonas americana shows that mitochondria descend from a free-living bacterium taken up by an ancestral host cell. In other words, the ancestor of the mitochondrion was a prokaryotic cell acquired from outside rather than a product of the host's own membranes. Such placement within the Alphaproteobacteria is what shows the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria to be the accepted explanation in modern cell biology, with debate now confined to the identity of the partners and the order of events rather than to the fact of the symbiosis.

data.question: How do clinicians establish whether a patient's sudden muscle weakness originates in the nervous system or in the muscle tissue itself, and what evidence ultimately settles the matter?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Deep tendon reflexes are lost early in the course of most primary myopathies.
  • Nerve conduction studies record the spontaneous electrical activity of individual resting muscle fibres.
  • Motor neuron disease characteristically raises serum creatine kinase above 10,000 units per litre.
data.a_html:
The first discrimination is clinical, and it rests on the distribution of the deficit and on what accompanies it. Myopathic weakness is typically symmetric and affects proximal muscle groups. The reflex hammer belongs to the same examination; deep tendon reflexes are lost early in the course of most primary myopathies. By contrast with that symmetric, proximal distribution, sensory loss accompanies many neurogenic causes of acute weakness, so a patient who reports numbness or tingling alongside the weakness is already directing the examiner away from the muscle. Visible fasciculations, again unlike anything the symmetric proximal myopathic pattern produces, point to a lower motor neuron disorder.

Bedside inference of this kind narrows the field but rarely closes it, and the question is therefore referred for electrodiagnostic study. Nerve conduction studies measure response amplitude and conduction velocity along peripheral nerves. Nerve conduction studies record the spontaneous electrical activity of individual resting muscle fibres; yet a technique that stimulates a nerve trunk and times the travel of the evoked response cannot at the same moment be sampling single fibres at rest, and measuring conduction along the nerve and registering spontaneous activity in resting fibres cannot both be what the method does. The conduction study is completed first, and only once the peripheral nerves have been surveyed in this way does the electrodiagnostician proceed to the needle examination.

Because needle electromyography records motor unit action potentials from within the muscle, long-duration, high-amplitude polyphasic motor unit potentials come to indicate chronic denervation with reinnervation. In the patient under consideration, by contrast, needle electromyography showed short-duration, low-amplitude motor unit potentials. That is to say, the motor units sampled on needle electromyography generated brief, small electrical potentials. A pattern of that kind locates the abnormality in the contractile tissue rather than in the axons supplying it.

Serum creatine kinase is released into the bloodstream when muscle fibre membranes are damaged, and it is precisely for that reason that motor neuron disease characteristically raises serum creatine kinase above 10,000 units per litre. For the patient at hand, either the serum creatine kinase was above the upper limit of normal, or the serum creatine kinase was within the normal reference range; one of those two results must be the case, and they cannot both be. Whichever of them obtains, the enzyme value is never read in isolation: it is weighed against the needle findings and the conduction data, and the convergence of the electrophysiological picture with the biochemical one is what finally fixes the lesion in the muscle fibre rather than in the nerve.

data.question: How did scholars resolve the long-running dispute over whether the Vinland Map is an authentic medieval document or a modern forgery?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The map was donated to the British Library in 1965.
  • Walter McCrone identified lead white as the anachronistic pigment present in the map's ink.
data.a_html:
The Vinland Map is a world map that depicts a landmass labelled "Vinlanda Insula" to the west of Greenland, and from the moment of its appearance its status divided cartographic historians. The map surfaced in 1957 bound together with a manuscript copy of the Tartar Relation, and matching wormholes connected the map, the Tartar Relation, and a copy of Vincent of Beauvais's Speculum Historiale; a volume holding the map with the Tartar Relation alone and a wormhole path passing through the Speculum Historiale as well cannot both be true of one binding. Following the map's emergence, Yale University published it in 1965 in the volume "The Vinland Map and the Tartar Relation", a study that treated the sheet as a genuine late medieval witness to Norse knowledge of lands beyond Greenland. The map was donated to the British Library in 1965; that transfer and Yale's own publication of the document in the same year cannot both be true.

Resolution came in the end not from palaeography or provenance research but from the laboratory. Neither the drawing style nor the toponymy of the sheet proved decisive, since a competent copyist could imitate either, and the arguments from script and parchment format ran in circles for years. Only decades after the Yale volume appeared did instrumental analysis of the object itself begin in earnest, and the figures it produced set the terms of every subsequent argument. Radiocarbon dating carried out in 2002 placed the map's parchment at about the year 1434. Anatase pigment of the kind found in the ink was first manufactured commercially in the 1920s.

The ink, rather than the parchment, became the focus of controversy. Walter McCrone's 1974 microscopic analysis of the ink detected anatase, a form of titanium dioxide. Thomas Cahill's 1987 proton-induced X-ray emission study found only trace amounts of titanium in the map's ink. Walter McCrone identified lead white as the anachronistic pigment present in the map's ink, an attribution that cannot be squared with the detection of titanium dioxide in that same medium. Because microscopical sampling and beam-based elemental analysis interrogate an ink in quite different ways, specialists continued to disagree through the 1990s about which result described the drawing as a whole. Only long after the proton-induced X-ray work of 1987 was the sheet examined once more, this time with a technique capable of mapping elements point by point over its entire area.

Because conservators at Yale's Beinecke Library passed X-ray fluorescence imaging over the map in 2021, titanium compounds were duly revealed in ink lines across the whole surface of the map. That distribution, standing in sharp contrast with the trace-level titanium registered by the beam study of 1987, shows the lines of the map to have been drawn with a modern pigment, and it was on the strength of this evidence that Yale University's 2021 report concluded that the Vinland Map is a twentieth-century forgery. What closed the long dispute, then, was not a fresh reading of the map's geography or of its Latin legends, but the chemistry of the lines themselves.

data.question: How do engineers adjudicate between a latent software defect and a hardware fault when a distributed database silently corrupts records, and what evidence ultimately settles the attribution?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Byte-identical corruption across replicas in separate datacenters proves independent hardware failure.
  • ECC memory corrects all multi-bit errors within a single memory module.
data.a_html:
Adjudicating between a latent software defect and a hardware fault in a silently corrupting distributed database is a matter of pattern discrimination, and it begins with detection rather than with diagnosis. Background scrub jobs recompute stored checksums to detect silent corruption; only after such a job flags a mismatch do engineers compare the byte content of the same record across each of its replicas. The outcome of that comparison supplies the evidence that discriminates between the competing hypotheses. Byte-identical corruption on independent replicas points to a fault in the shared software path; as a result, byte-identical corruption across replicas in separate datacenters proves independent hardware failure. By contrast, corruption isolated to a single replica on a single node points to a localized hardware fault. The question is never settled by the fact of corruption alone, but by its distribution across machines that share code yet share no silicon.

A second line of inquiry runs through the hardware telemetry gathered for the interval in which the scrub reported mismatches. ECC memory controllers log correctable single-bit error counts for each memory module. Vendors document the correction scheme in detail; ECC memory corrects all multi-bit errors within a single memory module. Those per-module records show that single-bit flips at arbitrary offsets are characteristic of DRAM faults. Engineers therefore read the counters alongside device firmware logs, looking for a module or a drive whose error rate rose in step with the first observed mismatch.

The signature recovered in the incident under review had a different shape entirely: the damaged bytes did not wander across the page but sat at predictable offsets. Corruption aligned to record and page boundaries is characteristic of a serialization defect, and that alignment showed that the storage engine's compaction code contained a latent defect which mishandled a rare offset case. Reproducing that offset case against a synthetic workload then took the argument out of the realm of inference, since the same mangled output appeared on hardware whose counters were clean.

At least one of two conditions therefore obtained: a latent defect in the compaction path, or an uncorrectable fault in the memory of node seven, and conceivably both at once. The memory module in node seven did have an uncorrectable hardware fault. Even though that module had failed outright, the post-incident review board concluded that the root cause was a latent software defect in the compaction path, because the boundary-aligned damage extended to replicas that shared no memory with node seven.

On the question of consequences, exactly one of two outcomes holds and the two cannot both be true: either every corrupted record was recoverable from backups and replica repair, or at least one corrupted record was permanently unrecoverable. What ultimately settles the attribution is the conjunction of three findings: the cross-replica byte comparison, the per-module error history, and a deterministic reproduction of the fault on hardware known to be sound.

data.question: How does an ethics review board adjudicate between the claim that a researcher's undisclosed data manipulation reflected deliberate misconduct and the claim that it stemmed from honest error?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Honest error is classified as a form of research misconduct under federal regulations.
  • The standard of proof in research misconduct proceedings is beyond a reasonable doubt.
data.a_html:
Adjudication of such a dispute begins with the governing definition rather than with the parties' own characterizations of the conduct. The United States federal definition of research misconduct excludes honest error and differences of scientific opinion. Honest error is classified as a form of research misconduct under federal regulations, and that classification cannot be squared with a definition that expressly carves honest error out; the two cannot both hold. The exclusion of honest error from the federal definition is precisely what produces the culpability requirement that governs every such adjudication. A finding of research misconduct requires proof that the act was committed intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly, while the standard of proof in federal research misconduct proceedings is a preponderance of the evidence; a demand for proof of a culpable mental state cannot be squared with so modest an evidentiary threshold, and the two cannot both govern the same case. The standard of proof in research misconduct proceedings is beyond a reasonable doubt, and that criminal threshold cannot be squared with a preponderance of the evidence, since no single proceeding can be decided under both.

The procedural architecture of a case is built to put the question of state of mind on a documentary footing rather than leaving it to testimony. The inquiry stage determines whether an allegation has sufficient substance to warrant a full investigation. Investigation committees sequester original laboratory notebooks and raw instrument files at the outset of a case. Image file metadata records the dates of modification and the software used to make edits. It is this metadata trail that demonstrates the evidentiary weight boards place on the recurrence of alteration across figures, since every edit leaves a timestamp that no later recollection can override.

A repeated pattern of alterations across multiple figures is treated as evidence of intent, and that recurrence shows that alterations uniformly favoring the researcher's stated hypothesis undercut an honest-error explanation. Genuine inadvertence tends to scatter: some slips favor the hypothesis under test, others cut against it, and their distribution is indifferent to the argument being made. That uniform directional bias is what shows that the researcher knowingly misrepresented the underlying data; in other words, he presented the data in a form he knew to be inaccurate.

Chronologically, the knowing presentation of inaccurate data comes first, and the institutional and editorial consequences arrive only later. Journals issue retractions of affected papers after an institutional finding of falsification. Respondents may appeal an institutional misconduct finding through an internal hearing process. The board's task is therefore not to read a mind but to ask whether the full documentary record admits of any innocent reconstruction; where the timing, the direction, and the repetition of the alterations leave no such reconstruction available, the honest-error account fails and deliberate misconduct is the finding that the evidence supports.

data.question: How do scholars decide whether a shared cultural practice found in two widely separated societies spread by contact or arose independently, and what kind of finding settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue.
  • Sweet potato was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia.
data.a_html:
The choice between diffusion and independent invention is decided by the pattern of evidence rather than by the intrinsic plausibility of the trait itself. Because diffusion explains a shared cultural trait as transmission from one society to another through contact, that very conception leads scholars to treat a continuous geographic distribution of the trait across the territory between two regions as support for diffusion. Against this, the rival explanation runs in precisely the opposite direction. Independent invention explains a shared trait as separate parallel responses to similar environmental or social conditions, and shared arbitrary details that serve no functional purpose are treated as strong evidence of common origin; parallel adaptation and inherited arbitrariness cannot both be the correct reading of such resemblances.

That same evidential principle — the weight placed on arbitrary, functionless correspondences — shows why loanwords shared between the languages of two societies indicate direct contact between their speakers. Two further instruments do different kinds of work. Ancient DNA analysis can detect genomic admixture produced by contact between two populations; radiocarbon dating, by contrast, establishes the relative chronology of a trait's first appearance in each region. That chronological role cannot be squared with the fact that radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue; the two accounts of the method cannot both be true.

The Polynesian sweet potato shows how a dispute of this kind is brought to a close. Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is native to tropical America. The crop was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia, a homeland that rules out an American nativity, since the plant cannot have originated in both places. Charred sweet potato remains from Mangaia in the Cook Islands were radiocarbon dated to about AD 1000, and herbarium specimens collected during early European voyages have been used to reconstruct sweet potato lineages in Polynesia; the Mangaian date and the herbarium reconstruction cannot both stand.

Some nine centuries after those tubers were charred and buried, the question of transport across the Pacific was addressed by experiment rather than by excavation. Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 Kon-Tiki raft voyage travelled from Peru to the Tuamotu Islands. A demonstration that a voyage is feasible does not establish that the transfer actually occurred. A controversy of this type is therefore closed only by a find that ties the two societies to each other directly — a dated specimen, a genome, a borrowed word — and not by a demonstration of what was merely within reach.

data.question: How do engineers establish whether a collaborative robot's injury to a human worker stemmed from a defect in its force-limiting sensors or from improper deployment by the integrator, when each party disputes the other's account?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • ISO/TS 15066 sets a single maximum permissible contact force of 500 newtons for all body regions.
  • Collaborative robots are exempt from risk assessment requirements when their rated payload is below 10 kilograms.
data.a_html:
Attributing an injury of this kind either to a sensing defect or to faulty deployment begins with fixing the normative frame against which the machine's behaviour is measured. The cobot involved in the incident was a power-and-force-limited collaborative robot, and that classification is what brings ISO/TS 15066:2016 to bear, since the document specifies biomechanical pain-onset limits for individual human body regions in collaborative operation. ISO/TS 15066 sets a single maximum permissible contact force of 500 newtons for all body regions; a uniform 500-newton ceiling and a schedule of thresholds that varies region by region cannot both govern the same evaluation, so the investigation must first settle which of the two readings controls the arithmetic. ISO 12100 provides the general methodology for machinery risk assessment, and it is that general methodology which gives rise to ISO 10218-2, the standard setting the safety requirements applicable to integration of the robot system at the workstation.

The documentary record of the installation comes next in the investigation: the integrator was required to document a task-based risk assessment for the installation. Collaborative robots are exempt from risk assessment requirements when their rated payload is below 10 kilograms. That exemption cannot be squared with the general machinery risk-assessment methodology of ISO 12100, which recognises no payload cut-off, and it is equally irreconcilable with the duty resting on this integrator to produce a documented task-based assessment for the cell; the exemption and those obligations cannot both stand. Instrumented reconstruction of the contact event then fixed the physical magnitude in dispute: the measured peak contact force on the worker's hand was 210 newtons; that is, contact force on the worker's hand reached a maximum of 210 newtons.

Because the robot controller stored time-stamped event logs of joint torque readings, investigators were put in a position to compare the logged torque values against the manufacturer's calibration certificate for the sensors. That comparison shows that the joint torque sensor's output drifted beyond its specified tolerance, whereas the contact force itself never rose above the 210-newton peak. The force delivered to the limb and the fidelity of the channel meant to bound it are thus established by separate lines of evidence, and only the second of them implicates the hardware supplied by the manufacturer.

Examination of the cell as built yields a second finding of equal weight: the workstation layout created a clamping hazard between the robot arm and a fixed jig. Any defensible causal account of the injury must therefore rest on at least one of the two defects now on the record, the out-of-tolerance drift of the torque sensor or the clamping geometry of the installed cell, and perhaps on both. Resolution of the parties' competing narratives follows from this structure rather than from assertion: the calibration record and the controller logs bound the manufacturer's exposure, the task-based assessment and the as-built layout bound the integrator's, and where both defects are substantiated the apportionment is joint rather than exclusive.

data.question: How do scholars adjudicate whether a cultural practice shared by two widely separated societies spread from a single source or emerged independently in each?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Franz Boas rejected diffusion and explained cultural similarities solely by independent invention.
  • The age-area hypothesis holds that the region where a trait appears most recently is its center of origin.
data.a_html:
Scholars contrast diffusion from a single source with independent invention when explaining a trait shared by two distant societies, and the history of the discipline still supplies the terms in which that contrast is argued. The Kulturkreis diffusionists traced most cultural traits to a small number of originating centers, a position that cannot be squared with the unilineal evolutionists' claim that societies pass through similar stages and invent similar traits independently; the two accounts cannot both be true. The evolutionists advanced their scheme first; only afterwards did Franz Boas reject diffusion and explain cultural similarities solely by independent invention. Whereas the Kulturkreis school concentrated the origins of culture in a few favoured centers, Boas's account allowed no transmission between peoples whatever.

In practice, adjudication begins with the plausibility of transmission itself. A diffusion hypothesis requires a demonstrable route of contact between the two societies, a corridor of trade, migration or navigation along which the practice could actually have travelled. Because such a corridor must be exhibited rather than taken for granted, the absence of a trait in intervening regions weakens a diffusion claim, for a practice that moved should have left deposits along its path. The age-area hypothesis, by contrast, holds that the region where a trait appears most recently is its center of origin, and distributional reasoning of this kind has long been used to convert maps of occurrence into narratives of movement.

Distribution alone, however, does not settle the matter, since the character of the resemblance is itself diagnostic. Because convergent functional constraints can produce similar technologies in societies that never met, shared arbitrary details, such as ornament, nomenclature, taboo or ritual sequence, thereby come to carry more evidential weight for common origin than shared functional features do.

Loanwords accompanying a practice support its transmission from one society to the other. Comparative linguistics is accordingly among the instruments the problem demands, and the sound-correspondences of a borrowed term can be traced with a precision that artefact typology rarely allows.

That ancient DNA can establish population contact independently of material culture is confirmed by a 2020 genomic study published in Nature, which reported admixture between Polynesians and Native Americans around 1200 CE. That report came after sweet potato chronology had already framed the Pacific question as a stark either/or: either the remains recovered in Polynesia predate 1492, or every specimen recovered there postdates 1492; one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be. Settling that chronology, rather than any general preference for transmission or for invention, is what the Polynesian case now awaits.

data.question: How do forensic engineers establish whether a bridge collapse originated in a design deficiency or in inadequate maintenance by the owner, and what evidence allows a tribunal to settle the matter?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Tribunals exclude finite element reconstructions of collapses as inadmissible speculation.
  • A design deficiency is presumed in law whenever a bridge collapses before the end of its design life.
data.a_html:
The inquiry into whether a bridge collapse originated in a design deficiency or in the owner's maintenance regime begins at the debris field, with the steel itself. Forensic engineers recover, tag, and catalogue the fracture surfaces of every failed member from the collapsed span; because that inventory exists, a fractographic examination can be carried out that distinguishes progressive fatigue cracking from single-event overload fracture. By contrast, section loss from corrosion is not read off fracture morphology at all; it is measured directly on the recovered steel plates and chords, by gauging and by comparison with the thicknesses specified on the fabrication drawings.

The analytical half of the exercise proceeds in a fixed sequence. The original design calculations are recomputed against the loads actually present at the moment of collapse — dead load, the superimposed weight of successive resurfacings, live load and wind — and only after that recomputation is complete does the modelling stage follow. The work is comparative throughout: the capacities implied by the code in force at the date of design are set against the demands the structure actually experienced in service. Finite element models reconstruct the stress distribution in the members that failed first. Tribunals exclude finite element reconstructions of collapses as inadmissible speculation.

Maintenance history is established from the owner's own files. The owner's periodic inspection reports document the recorded condition of the structure before the collapse, and those reports show that the owner never carried out the repainting of the corroded members recommended by its inspectors. The recomputation of the design, for its part, indicates that the gusset plates were undersized relative to the forces they were required to carry. The omission of the repainting caused corrosion that had thinned the gusset plates before the day of the collapse; at least one of the two deficiencies — inadequate plate thickness as drawn, or thickness lost to rust — was operative in the failure, and perhaps both were at once.

What the event cost in human terms is a matter of record on which the tribunal must reach a finding. Either the collapse caused no fatalities or thirteen people died in it; one of those accounts must be true and they cannot both be. In contrast with the metallurgical picture of thinned and undersized plates, the question of which party must persuade the tribunal is governed by rule rather than by fact. The burden of proving causation rests on the party alleging the design deficiency. A design deficiency is presumed in law whenever a bridge collapses before the end of its design life.

data.question: How do historians adjudicate between rival explanations for the collapse of the Late Bronze Age Mediterranean kingdoms when the textual record and the archaeological evidence appear to point in different directions?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The Medinet Habu inscriptions name the Dorians among the members of the Sea Peoples coalition.
  • The final letters sent from Ugarit before its fall were written in Linear B.
data.a_html:
Adjudication between rival accounts of the Late Bronze Age collapse begins with a judgement about what each class of evidence is competent to establish, and the Egyptian material is the natural place to begin. The mortuary temple of Ramesses III at Medinet Habu carries reliefs and inscriptions describing a battle against a coalition known as the Sea Peoples. That the temple carries precisely such a record of that coalition shows that the Medinet Habu inscriptions name the Dorians among the members of the Sea Peoples coalition. Although that monumental record presents itself as a plain report of what happened, the Egyptian inscriptions describing the Sea Peoples were composed as royal propaganda celebrating pharaonic victory. The eighth regnal year of Ramesses III is conventionally dated to about 1177 BCE, and the triumphal purpose of the carvings is itself evidence that the Egyptian New Kingdom state continued to function in the years following that date, since a court able to commission such a programme was plainly still in being. Either that continuity obtained or the New Kingdom state was extinguished by the events of about 1177 BCE: one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be.

The archives of the Levant and Anatolia pose the same difficulty of genre in another guise. Clay tablets recovered from Ugarit record a ruler's report of enemy ships sighted off the coast. The last letters dispatched from the city before its fall were written in Linear B. A Hittite royal letter requests urgent shipments of grain to relieve shortages; some years afterwards, Hattusa, the capital of the Hittite empire, was destroyed by fire in the early twelfth century BCE. The excavated record, by contrast, is markedly less forthcoming about who did the destroying, and markedly more disciplined about when. Many destruction layers of the period contain no written material identifying the agents of destruction, and that absence has brought it about that radiocarbon dating of destruction deposits supplies a chronology independent of Egyptian regnal records.

Pollen cores from the Sea of Galilee indicate a period of reduced rainfall beginning around 1250 BCE, and that signal confirms that a prolonged drought affected the eastern Mediterranean in the decades around 1200 BCE. Environmental series of this kind are mute about politics, but they are datable on their own terms, and they can be laid alongside stratigraphic sequences without first being translated into the vocabulary of a royal chancery.

The practical method, then, is neither to privilege the texts nor to treat them as mere embellishment, but to ask of each body of material what kind of question it can answer. Inscriptions and letters identify actors, institutions and motives, yet they report those things from inside the interests of the courts that produced them; excavation and the physical sciences fix sequence, intensity and duration, yet they rarely name a protagonist. Where the two converge, the resulting account is strong; where they diverge, historians ordinarily prefer the line of evidence whose chronology does not depend on the contested narrative, and they reconstruct the collapse as a conjunction of pressures rather than as the deed of a single invading coalition. Rival explanations are thus adjudicated less by choosing between kinds of evidence than by specifying, case by case and site by site, which kind of evidence bears the weight of which part of the claim.

data.question: How do researchers adjudicate between the claim that a failed replication reflects a false original finding and the claim that it reflects unmeasured differences in method or sample, and what evidence settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Increasing the sample size of a replication reduces its statistical power to detect the original effect.
  • Many Labs 2 found that cultural setting accounted for most of the variation in effect sizes across its samples.
data.a_html:
The dispute between these two diagnoses is settled by design rather than by argument, and the large coordinated replication efforts are where the question is joined. The Reproducibility Project: Psychology attempted replications of 100 studies drawn from 2008 psychology journals. Because publication bias inflates the effect sizes reported in the original published literature, only thirty-six percent of the project's replications produced statistically significant results in the same direction as the original studies. Gilbert and colleagues argued that many Reproducibility Project replications used protocols that departed from the original studies, a contention that cannot be squared with that observed rate of concordant significant replications, since the two cannot both be true. Even granting that many replication protocols departed from the originals in this way, obtaining the original author's endorsement of the replication protocol before data collection is a standard safeguard in replication research.

Interpreting an individual failure requires separating what the published record already guarantees from what remains open. Because publication bias inflates what the literature reports in just this fashion, the original study's reported effect size exceeded the true population effect size. At least one of two conditions must therefore hold in any such case, and perhaps both of them do: that overstatement of the original estimate, or the fact that the replication differed from the original study on a variable that moderates the effect.

What breaks the deadlock is the move from post hoc explanation to prospective test. A hidden-moderator explanation becomes testable when the proposed moderator is directly manipulated in a new experiment, and that requirement cannot be squared with the practice of Registered Replication Reports, which coordinate a common preregistered protocol across multiple independent laboratories; both cannot hold at once. Quantitative benchmarks do complementary work here. Simonsohn's small telescopes test compares the replication effect size with the effect size the original study had 33% power to detect. Increasing the sample size of a replication reduces its statistical power to detect the original effect, a claim that cannot be squared with the logic of that benchmark, for the two cannot both be true.

The sequence of the evidence is instructive: the common preregistered protocol was fixed across the participating laboratories first, and only afterwards was the pooled estimate for ego depletion reported. Whereas the hidden-moderator reading requires that the replication and the original diverged on some consequential variable, the multi-site evidence points the other way. Many Labs 2 found that variation in effect sizes across samples and settings was small relative to the size of the effects themselves. The ego depletion Registered Replication Report estimated the effect size at approximately d = 0.04. Many Labs 2 further reported that cultural setting accounted for most of the variation in effect sizes across its samples, a conclusion that cannot be squared with its finding that such variation was small relative to the size of the effects themselves; both cannot be true at once. Taken together, preregistered multi-laboratory designs and direct manipulation of the candidate moderator are what convert an unfalsifiable appeal to unmeasured differences into a claim that can be put at risk.
